In \(\triangle ACD\):
\[
\angle ADC=180^\circ-60^\circ-23^\circ=97^\circ.
\]
By the sine rule,
\[
\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{\sin 23^\circ}{\sin 97^\circ}.
\]
Since \(AB+AD=AC\),
\[
\frac{AB}{AC}=1-\frac{\sin 23^\circ}{\sin 97^\circ}
=\frac{\sin 97^\circ-\sin 23^\circ}{\sin 97^\circ}.
\]
Using \(\sin 97^\circ-\sin 23^\circ=2\cos 60^\circ\sin 37^\circ=\sin 37^\circ\),
\[
\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{\sin 37^\circ}{\sin 97^\circ}
=\frac{\sin 37^\circ}{\sin 83^\circ}.
\]

In \(\triangle ABC\), let \(\angle ABC=\beta\). Then \(\angle ACB=120^\circ-\beta\). By the sine rule,
\[
\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{\sin(120^\circ-\beta)}{\sin\beta}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{\sin(120^\circ-\beta)}{\sin\beta}
=\frac{\sin 37^\circ}{\sin 83^\circ}.
\]
So \(\beta=83^\circ\).

\[
\boxed{83^\circ}
\]
